title: Netflix Confirms Renewals for UK Fan Favourites and Debuts Trailer for 'The Gentlemen' Season 2
summary: Netflix today confirmed new season renewals for some of its most-loved UK titles.
body_markdown:
Entertainment


23 August 2026


Global


United Kingdom


Link copied to clipboard


### Netflix today confirmed new season renewals for some of its most-loved UK titles. From returning drama to unscripted favourites, the slate spans the breadth of what UK audiences have turned into hits.


> Anne Mensah, Vice President, UK Content, said:
>
>
> “Our audiences loved these shows so it is such a delight to bring them back. To revisit the Guinness family, cook with the Ramsays, go undercover with the Legends and be
>
>
> At Home With The Furys.
>
>
> A huge thank you to the brilliant producers, actors, writers, directors and crew behind these shows and all of our returners on Netflix — it’s an utter privilege to host these gems.”


To coincide with the news that


The Gentlemen


will be returning for a third season, Netflix has also released the full-length trailer for Guy Ritchie’s


The Gentlemen:


Season 2, launching 3 September 2026 on Netflix.


##### LIST OF CONFIRMED RENEWALS INCLUDE:


The Gentlemen


- Season 3


: Netflix can officially confirm the hit series of


The Gentlemen


will be back for a third season, with Guy Ritchie once again directing.


> Creator, writer, director and executive producer Guy Ritchie said:
>
>
> “The ambition of
>
>
> The Gentlemen
>
>
> has accelerated, the world has expanded and the consequences carry weight. A third season felt inevitable, and I’m looking forward to pushing the boundaries of it further.”


---


Legends


– Season 2


: Neil Forsyth’s undercover customs thriller is confirmed to return. The second series of


Legends


will go into production in 2027.


> Neil Forsyth, writer and creator of
>
>
> Legends
>
>
> , said:
>
>
> “I'm delighted to have the opportunity to tell a new story in the fascinating and unique world that Legends offers, and to show just how dangerous, thrilling, and important their work became in the late 1990s.”


---


House of Guinness


– Season 2:


Steven Knight's decadent 19th-century Dublin drama returns for a second season, following the Guinness Family as they wrestle with ambition, intrigue and forbidden love. Production is due to begin in early 2027.


> Steven Knight, writer and creator of
>
>
> House of Guinness,
>
>
> said:
>
>
> “It was such a joy to bring the Guinness story to the screen, so I'm beyond thrilled to be continuing the story of one of the world's greatest dynasties into season two. I can't wait to dive deeper into these characters and their complex relationships as they expand the Guinness empire.”


---


Being Gordon Ramsay


– Season 2


: Gordon Ramsay welcomes us back inside his hectic world & restaurant empire for a second time, as he balances his ever-expanding business ventures with family life.


---


Formula 1: Drive to Survive


– Season 9


: Formula 1’s behind-the-scenes docuseries returns for a ninth season, capturing the drama of the 2026 grid.


> James Gay-Rees & Paul Martin, executive producers at Box to Box, said:
>
>
> “We’re so excited to be making Season 9 of this iconic show. This year we’re going to go deeper than ever before into the hidden spaces of this fantastic sport.”


---


This comes off the back of a number of UK commissioned renewals including:


-


Love Is Blind: UK


– Season 4


: Hosted by Matt and Emma Willis,


Love Is Blind: UK


has been renewed for a fourth season with a fresh group of hopeful singles, ahead of the launch of Season 3 later this summer.


-


The Rest Is Football


:


Gary Lineker, Alan Shearer and Micah Richards return to Netflix for the 2026/27 Premier League season, bringing their trademark blend of expert analysis, unfiltered debate, the biggest football talking points and plenty of laughs. Episodes will premiere every Monday and Friday throughout the season, alongside a brand-new exclusive episode every Sunday evening, giving fans a quick take on the major headlines from the weekend’s action. The new Sunday night show premiered for the first time last night, marking an exciting new addition to


The Rest Is Football’s


weekly schedule.


> Gary Lineker on what fans can expect, taken from last night’s first episode:
>
>
> “The new season is underway, and we're back on Netflix to follow all the trials and tribulations as Arsenal aim to defend their Premier League crown. This year, we've got an extra episode each week, which you can only get on Netflix. Every Sunday, we're going to pick our story of the weekend, where we'll get together immediately after the final game for a quick chat about the biggest headlines… Each Sunday, Harry (producer) will be with myself, Alan, or Micah, as we debate the biggest story of the weekend and give our immediate take on the action in this short recap.”


-


At Home With The Furys


– Season 3


: The Fury family’s hit reality series returns and is currently in production, following the family’s move to the Isle of Man, Venezuela’s marriage to Noah Price and the warmth, humour and unpredictability of everyday life inside the Fury household.


-


Black Mirror


- Season 8:


Charlie Brooker’s critically acclaimed


Black Mirror


started production on Season 8 this summer


-


Supacell


- Season 2:


Rapman’s Bafta award-winning


Supacell


, about a group of five ordinary people who unexpectedly develop superpowers, has just wrapped on Season 2. Launch date to be confirmed.


-


Black Doves


- Season 2:


Joe Barton’s British spy thriller starring Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw, Sarah Lancashire and Ambika Mod is set to return later this year.
